title: North Warren football coach thinking long term | State of the Program - NewsBreak
text: Usually, a new football coach means many changes during summer practice. But at North Warren, John Baum waited a year before he started tweaking things. The young Patriots got just one victory last fall, 34-26 against winless Hopatcong . But most are back after facing varsity competition as sophomores. Baum plans to use a more traditional Wing-T this fall, using techniques learned from retired Lenape Valley legend Don Smolyn and his cousin, longtime Morris County football coach Cosmo Lorusso. The goal is to simplify and streamline getting the ball to senior backs Aiden Able and A.J. Soricelli. "We want to hammer out the specific plays we want to run offensively," said Baum, a former Patriots tight end and defensive end. "As long as we're blocking up front, and our skill guys are going the direction we want to go, we should be in good shape." But North Warren has low turnout again, with around 30 players at summer workouts. Baum adjusted the summer practice schedule, going Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and the occasional Saturday. That gives players four-day weekends, and the mandatory blackout period right before official camp starts on Aug. 11. North Warren played a pair of 7-on-7s with Morris Hills in mid-July. The Patriots also beefed up their offseason lifting program, and added more summer conditioning. The goal is to build endurance, and avoid faltering late in games. "They saw what was going on last year, and they wanted to change. I wanted to change," Baum said. "I got my feet wet last year. Now I have an opportunity to make things more my own, and put my own stamp on the program." North Warren had its most recent winning seasons in 2022 and a four-year stretch in the 2010s when Matt Parzero – now the longtime Newton coach – was at the helm. The Patriots have not won a playoff game since 2013, and have never reached a sectional final. Baum is thinking long term, with a goal of having 35 to 40 on the high school roster every year. He's working with coaches in the North Warren feeder program to make sure all levels are using the same formations and terminology. There aren't many players at the seventh- and eighth-grade level, but flag has 30 or 40 kids. North Warren is hosting youth football players and cheerleaders at the home opener against Wallkill Valley on Sept. 5. The kids all get free entry into the game and a free hot dog. They'll welcome the varsity Patriots when they walk onto the field, and the young cheerleaders will perform at halftime alongside the high school squad. "It'll open their eyes wide, hopefully, and get them excited to get up here," said Baum, a father of two young children. "I want the community to be excited again, to come out on a Friday night and see some good football." North Warren has a tri-scrimmage scheduled with Sussex Tech and South Hunterdon on Aug. 23, before a Week Zero game at Bound Brook. That was added late, because Baum felt like the Patriots got off to a slow start in their first division game – a 23-8 loss at Wallkill Valley – last fall.
